short: A cost incurred but not yet billed or paid.
seoTitle: Accrued Expense — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: A cost incurred but not yet billed or paid. Comparisons between months become meaningless. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: An accrued expense is a cost the business has already incurred but has not yet been billed or paid for — electricity consumed, salaries earned, or interest accumulated at period end.
bodyHtml:
Why Accrued Expense matters

Leaving accruals out makes a month look more profitable than it was, and dumps the cost into whichever month the bill happens to arrive. Comparisons between months become meaningless.

How Accrued Expense works in practice

At each period end, list costs consumed but not invoiced, post them as accruals, and reverse them when the actual bill arrives. Rent, utilities, salaries and interest are the usual four.

Worked example

March electricity billed in April is accrued in March, so March carries the cost it actually consumed.

faq.question: What is the difference between an accrual and a provision?
faq.answer: An accrual is a known cost awaiting its bill; a provision is an estimate for an obligation whose amount is uncertain.

faq.question: Do I need accruals for a small business?
faq.answer: For meaningful monthly comparison, yes — at least for the large recurring costs.
